**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected:** Wheat/grass leaves
- **Key features:**
  - Orange-brown powdery pustules (uredinia) scattered across the leaf surface
  - Pustules are small, round to oval, and raised — clearly erupting through the epidermis
  - Orange/brick-red spore masses visible, especially concentrated along the leaf midrib and lower leaf
  - Surrounding leaf tissue shows some yellowing/chlorosis
  - Pustules appear randomly distributed (not in stripes/rows)
  - The orange color and round pustule arrangement on the leaf blade is characteristic

**Reasoning:**

- The orange, randomly scattered circular pustules on the leaf surface strongly indicate a **leaf rust** (not stripe rust, which forms in stripes/rows; not stem rust, which forms on stems/sheaths with larger, darker pustules)
- Stripe rust (*Puccinia striiformis*) produces yellow-orange pustules arranged in linear stripes along the leaf veins
- Stem rust (*Puccinia graminis*) produces larger, darker (reddish-brown), elongated pustules mainly on stems
- **Wheat Leaf Rust** (*Puccinia triticina*) produces small, round, orange-brown uredinia randomly scattered on the upper leaf surface — exactly matching this image
- The brick-orange color, small round shape, and random distribution across the leaf lamina is the textbook presentation of wheat leaf rust
